title: 숙명여대 편입영어 모의고사
source: 숙명여대 편입영어 2023~2026학년도 기출 출제 유형(문항 수·영역·문제 꼴, VocabFactory 분석)을 분석해 dailyfreetoolbox 가 새로 만든 연습 문제

passages.text: Once we have acquired a piece of knowledge, it becomes remarkably difficult to recall what ignorance felt like. Psychologists label this cognitive bias the curse of knowledge. In a celebrated study from 1990, one group of participants tapped out the rhythm of a familiar song, such as Happy Birthday, while listeners attempted to identify the tune. The tappers confidently forecast that listeners would recognize about half of the songs. In reality, listeners identified only about one in forty. The tappers could hear the melody resonating in their heads; the listeners perceived nothing but a disjointed series of knocks. The same discrepancy besets experts of every stripe. Engineers compose manuals that omit steps they deem self-evident, and teachers deploy jargon their pupils have never encountered, each oblivious to how much their own expertise tacitly fills in the missing pieces.

In October 2024, the Swedish Academy announced that the South Korean novelist Han Kang had been awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She thereby became the first Korean author to garner the honor and the first Asian woman to do so. The Academy singled out the poetic intensity of her prose, which confronts historical trauma and lays bare the fragility of human life. Han was hardly unknown to readers abroad, since her novel The Vegetarian, in Deborah Smith's English translation, had captured the Man Booker International Prize in 2016. At home, the announcement sparked a frenzy: bookstores reported that her titles sold out almost instantaneously, and publishers scrambled to replenish their depleted stock. The accolade also drew renewed attention to literary translators, whose painstaking labor had carried Korean fiction overseas.

Across affluent nations, women now constitute nearly half of the paid workforce, yet the hours they devote to unpaid care have diminished far less than many anticipated. Cooking, cleaning, and tending to children or frail parents still fall (A) ____ on women, even when both partners work full-time. Sociologists dub this burden the second shift. Because caregiving makes long or erratic hours untenable, many mothers retreat into part-time or lower-paid positions, and the disparity between men's and women's earnings tends to widen markedly after the birth of a first child. Parental leave earmarked for fathers and affordable childcare can alleviate the strain, but researchers caution that their efficacy hinges on whether workplaces (B) ____ the employees who use them or tacitly penalize them. Unpaid care, in short, is no mere private matter; it shapes how an economy harnesses the talents of half its population.

In 2020, East Africa suffered its worst desert locust outbreak in decades. Desert locusts lead a peculiar double life. Most of the time they behave like innocuous grasshoppers: shy, solitary, and camouflaged to blend into the arid scrub they inhabit. When torrential rains spur a burst of vegetation and the land dries out again, however, the insects are compelled to congregate on the few remaining patches of green. Repeated contact with one another's hind legs triggers a drastic metamorphosis. Within hours, the insects become drawn to company rather than shunning it, and over subsequent generations they acquire vivid coloring and sturdier flight muscles. Researchers have traced the initial step of this transformation to a surge in serotonin, a chemical messenger in the nervous system. The upshot can be a voracious swarm of billions, capable of stripping the crops of entire regions within days.

In 2022, the member states of the United Nations resolved to negotiate the first global treaty on plastic pollution, aiming to finalize it by late 2024. The final scheduled round of talks, convened in Busan, South Korea, in late 2024, collapsed without an accord, as did a further session in Geneva in August 2025. The central point of contention concerns where the treaty should begin. Many countries maintain that the world cannot simply recycle its way out of the predicament and that curbs on the production of new plastic ____ indispensable. Several major oil- and petrochemical-producing nations, by contrast, insist that the treaty should confine itself to waste management and recycling, leaving production to the discretion of each government. Whatever its eventual shape, any agreement is apt to be judged less by its ambition on paper than by whether governments are amenable to enforcing it.

On my third day at the design firm, I was summoned to a meeting with a prominent client. I had prepared nothing, presuming a newcomer would merely listen. Midway through, the client turned to me and solicited my opinion of the logo my team had proposed. My manager offered a subtle, reassuring nod, and I realized there was no evading the question. I ventured that I found the color too somber for a children's brand. A prolonged silence ensued, and I was convinced I had jeopardized everything. The client then chuckled and confessed that she had harbored the same reservation. Afterward, my manager told me I had <u>broken the ice</u> for the rest of the team, who had shared my misgivings but had not dared to voice them. A candid opinion, tactfully offered, is seldom as perilous as it feels.

In a lecture delivered in Paris in 1945, the philosopher Jean-Paul Sartre distilled existentialism into a terse formula: existence precedes essence. Consider a manufactured artifact such as a paper knife. Its maker knows its purpose before it is fashioned, so its essence comes first. Sartre contended that human beings are fundamentally different. There is no immutable human nature that dictates what each of us must become. We first exist and find ourselves thrust into the world, and only afterward define ourselves through the choices we make.
This can sound exhilarating, but Sartre insisted that it is also an onerous burden. If there is no predetermined nature to blame, we cannot excuse our conduct by invoking our temperament, our upbringing, or our circumstances. Even refusing to choose is itself a choice for which we remain accountable. Sartre called the attempt to evade this freedom, feigning that we had no alternative, bad faith.
Critics have objected that Sartre ____ the weight of social conditions, such as poverty or discrimination, which can severely circumscribe the options available to a person. In his later writings, Sartre himself paid greater heed to such constraints. Yet his argument still resonates with readers who refuse to believe their lives are scripted.

When the drama Squid Game became Netflix's most-watched series in 2021, many pundits dismissed it as a lucky fluke. Few would say so today. Korean films, dramas, and music now captivate audiences on every continent. In 2025, an animated film about a fictional K-pop girl group who covertly hunt demons became one of the most-watched films in Netflix's history. That film, notably, was produced by an American studio rather than a Korean one. Its triumph suggests that the K in K-content now denotes a recognizable style, with polished visuals, emotional storytelling, and close ties between music and fandom, rather than a country of origin. Some in the Korean industry ____ this development as proof of their culture's reach; others fret that profits and creative control may increasingly migrate elsewhere. Whether that shift helps Korea will depend on who owns the stories.

Why do people demand more to relinquish an object than they would pay to acquire it? In a classic experiment, half the students in a class were given coffee mugs emblazoned with their university's logo and invited to sell them, while the other half could purchase them. Because the mugs had been distributed at random, economic theory predicted that roughly half of them would change hands. Instead, trades were rare. Owners typically demanded more than twice as much for a mug as buyers were willing to pay. Psychologists term this anomaly the endowment effect: mere ownership appears to inflate an object's value. The effect helps explain why free trial periods prove so lucrative for businesses, and why people cling to possessions they seldom use. Streaming services and software makers, for instance, commonly let customers use a product free for a month before billing them.

Most animals follow an irreversible trajectory from birth to maturity to death. A tiny jellyfish called Turritopsis dohrnii appears to defy that sequence. When it is injured, starved, or otherwise stressed, the adult medusa can sink to the seabed, reabsorb its tentacles, and (A) ____ to a polyp. This is the juvenile stage from which jellyfish ordinarily develop. That polyp grows into a colony, budding genetically identical medusae over time. The phenomenon was first documented in the late 1980s by a German student examining specimens collected off the Italian coast. Because the cycle can in principle recur indefinitely, the creature is dubbed the immortal jellyfish. The label is somewhat (B) ____, however: in the wild, most individuals are devoured by predators or succumb to disease long before they have any opportunity to rejuvenate.

In August 2024, South Korea's Constitutional Court ruled that the national climate law failed to safeguard the rights of future generations. The petition had been brought in part by young activists, some still in school, contending that the law set a target for 2030 but was silent about the decades that followed. The court concurred that the absence of targets beyond 2030 was unconstitutional and ordered the National Assembly to amend the law by February 2026. The verdict, widely hailed as the first of its kind in Asia, ____ to a burgeoning body of climate litigation worldwide. A year earlier, a court in Montana had sided with sixteen young plaintiffs who challenged the state's promotion of fossil fuels. Such rulings seldom dictate precise policies, but they establish that a government's failure to plan for the future can itself contravene fundamental rights.

Most stories implicitly invite us to trust the person telling them. An unreliable narrator violates that tacit pact. The term was coined by the critic Wayne Booth in 1961 to describe narrators whose accounts the reader gradually learns to distrust, whether because they lie, misconstrue events, or lack insight into themselves. In Edgar Allan Poe's story The Tell-Tale Heart, the speaker repeatedly insists that he is perfectly sane, recounting a murder in feverish detail. His very insistence becomes the most damning evidence against him. Kazuo Ishiguro's The Remains of the Day offers a subtler example. An aging butler recounts his years of service with dignified restraint, yet the reader gradually discerns a regret he cannot bring himself to articulate. Such narrators turn reading into detective work: the pleasure lies in spotting the gap between what the narrator asserts and what the story reveals.

"You don't have to say yes to everything," a colleague cautioned me during my first month at the newspaper. I ignored her. When the sports editor solicited help with a weekend feature, I agreed. When the night desk was short of a copy editor, I volunteered. When a reporter fell ill, I offered to complete his story on the municipal budget. By the third week I was subsisting on five hours of sleep, producing articles that had grown perfunctory. The low point came when I misspelled the mayor's name in a headline, a blunder thousands of readers noticed before breakfast. My colleague never said she had warned me; she simply helped me list what I had promised. I had <u>bitten off more than I could chew</u>, and learning to decline turned out to be as indispensable as learning to write.

When fire ravaged the roof of Notre-Dame de Paris in April 2019, restorers found an unforeseen ally. Years earlier, the art historian Andrew Tallon had used lasers to scan the cathedral in minute detail, yielding a record accurate to a few millimeters. His data became one of many resources that guided the reconstruction, and the cathedral reopened in December 2024. The episode is often cited as a reason to digitize heritage early.
Spurred by other motives, museums have embraced the idea too. In 2020, the Smithsonian Institution released millions of images from its collections for anyone to reuse free of charge, and other eminent museums have followed suit. A student in an isolated village can now examine a painting more closely than a visitor in the gallery.
Digitization, however, is neither cheap nor permanent. File formats become obsolete, servers malfunction, and the expense of maintaining digital archives persists long after a project ends. Some curators caution that an impeccable image on a screen may foster the belief that an object need not be seen in person, or even preserved, once a replica exists. A digital record, they contend, is valuable only if it is treated as insurance for the original, not a substitute.

Linger a few minutes in a bath and the skin on your fingers and toes becomes wrinkled. For decades, this was presumed to be a matter of skin absorbing water and swelling. Yet the wrinkling does not occur if the nerves to the fingers have been damaged, which indicates that it is an active response orchestrated by the nervous system: blood vessels beneath the skin constrict, and the surface buckles. Why would the body bother? One conjecture is that wrinkled fingertips function like the treads on a tire, channeling water away and bolstering grip on slippery surfaces. In a 2013 experiment, volunteers with wrinkled fingers transferred wet marbles from one container to another faster than those with smooth fingers. A subsequent study, however, detected no such advantage, and the question remains a conundrum.

In late 2024, the publisher of the Oxford dictionaries crowned brain rot its word of the year, a phrase for the cognitive deterioration supposedly induced by endless scrolling. The choice crystallized a pervasive anxiety. Concurrently, an international survey of adult skills by the OECD reported that literacy had declined or stagnated in most participating countries over the preceding decade. Korea has had its own vigorous debate, fueled by viral incidents in which readers misconstrued common words in public notices. Some pundits blame ubiquitous short videos and smartphones for eroding the patience that lengthy texts demand. Others caution against ____, pointing out that every generation has accused the next of reading less attentively, and that young people today write and read a great many words each day, albeit mostly in messages and posts. The evidence does suggest that sustained reading, like any skill, atrophies without practice.

In December 2024, UNESCO inscribed Korea's tradition of jang-making on its list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Jang denotes a family of fermented soybean products, including the soy sauce ganjang and the soybean paste doenjang, that remain indispensable to Korean cuisine. The process commences with boiled soybeans molded into blocks called meju, which are dried and fermented before being steeped in brine. Months later, the liquid is drawn off to become sauce, while the residual solids become paste. What UNESCO recognized was not the food itself but the knowledge and customs surrounding it, handed down within families and communities, along with the communal labor that accompanies preparation. The listing succeeded an earlier one for kimjang, the collective making of kimchi for winter, inscribed in 2013.

The last bus to the coast had already departed when I reached the terminal, my rucksack still dripping from the afternoon downpour. I had meticulously planned the trip for months and stood there furious with myself for dawdling over lunch. An elderly vendor peddling tangerines outside the terminal asked where I was headed. When I told her, she shook her head and explained that the coastal road had been blocked by a landslide an hour earlier; the bus I had missed would be stranded for the night. She then phoned her nephew, who ran a modest guesthouse nearby, and I spent the evening savoring grilled fish with his family and memorizing the names of the surrounding peaks. The next morning the road reopened, and I reached the coast by noon. Missing that bus, I realized, had been <u>a blessing in disguise</u>.

In December 2022, nearly two hundred governments convening in Montreal adopted an accord to arrest the loss of nature. Its best-known goal, 30 by 30, commits countries to conserve at least 30 percent of the planet's land and 30 percent of its oceans by 2030. The target is (A) ____. According to a 2024 United Nations report, only about 17 percent of land and 8 percent of the oceans were protected, so the protected share of the seas would need to more than triple within a few years. Proponents argue that an audacious number galvanizes attention and funding. Critics retort that numbers alone can mislead, since some protected areas exist largely on paper, with scant funding or enforcement. Indigenous groups also insist on respect for local rights, since many of the best-preserved ecosystems are already (B) ____ by communities who have nurtured them for generations. Much will depend on funding.

For years, consumers have lamented that defective appliances are cheaper to replace than to repair. In 2024 the European Union enacted a directive intended to alter that calculus. It obliges manufacturers of certain everyday products, including washing machines, refrigerators, vacuum cleaners, and mobile phones, to offer repairs at a reasonable price even after the legal guarantee has lapsed. Consumers who opt for repair over replacement during the guarantee period ____ an extra year of coverage. The rules also establish a European online platform to help people locate nearby repair shops. Member states have until mid-2026 to transpose the directive into national law. Proponents hope the measure will reduce electronic waste and bolster small repair businesses, but some manufacturers warn that stocking spare parts for years will inflate their costs. Whether repair truly becomes the cheaper option will depend on how strictly the rules are enforced.

Between 1751 and 1772, the French writer Denis Diderot and his collaborators published the Encyclopédie, among the most ambitious books of its century. Its seventeen volumes of text and eleven volumes of illustrations aimed to amass human knowledge and render it accessible to ordinary educated readers. Its subtitle promised a reasoned dictionary of the sciences, arts, and trades.
That last word was pivotal. Alongside articles on philosophy and mathematics, the Encyclopédie lavished attention on crafts such as weaving, printing, and glassmaking, with meticulous plates depicting tools and workshops. By treating the expertise of artisans as worthy of rigorous study, it implicitly challenged a social order that belittled manual work.
Its other challenges were less subtle. Some articles impugned the authority of the Church and the monarchy, often obliquely, through cross-references that led a curious reader from an innocuous entry to a subversive one. The authorities suspended publication in 1752 and revoked its license in 1759, yet Diderot persisted in producing the remaining volumes of text clandestinely.
Historians still dispute how far the Encyclopédie paved the way for the French Revolution. What is clearer is that it embodied a novel conviction: that knowledge belongs not to a privileged few but to anyone willing to read.

밑줄 친 말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
The senator's <u>grandiloquent</u> tribute to the retiring clerk, packed with classical allusions, ran for twenty minutes and left the audience glancing at their watches.
grandiloquent 는 '말을 거창하게 부풀리는'이라 grand and showy 가 맞아요. 고전 인용을 잔뜩 넣어 20분이나 이어졌다는 설명이 단서이고, plain and simple 과 brief and direct 는 반대예요.

밑줄 친 말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
Critics dismissed the restaurant's <u>ersatz</u> village décor, with its plastic vines and painted stone walls, as a shoddy substitute for the genuine countryside.
ersatz 는 '진짜를 흉내 낸, 대용의'라 cheap and artificial 이 맞아요. 플라스틱 덩굴, 그려 넣은 돌벽, 진짜 시골의 '형편없는 대용품'이라는 말이 단서이고 real and genuine 은 반대예요.

밑줄 친 말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
Visitors anticipating a <u>placid</u> lake were surprised to find the water churning with waves whipped up by abrupt afternoon gusts from the mountains.
placid 는 '잔잔하고 평온한'이라 calm and peaceful 이 맞아요. rough and stormy 는 실제로 본 거친 물결 쪽이라 반대예요.

밑줄 친 말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
The new director disliked <u>subservient</u> staff who agreed with every suggestion simply to avoid displeasing anyone above them.
subservient 는 '지나치게 굽실거리며 따르는'이라 obedient and submissive 가 맞아요. 윗사람 기분을 거스르지 않으려고 모든 제안에 동의한다는 설명이 단서이고, independent and bold 와 critical and outspoken 은 반대예요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
The number of passengers who board overnight trains across Europe ____ steadily over the past decade, according to figures compiled by the national statistics agency.
주어는 The number(~의 수) 하나라 단수 has 가 오고, over the past decade 가 있어 현재완료 has risen 이 맞아요. rise 는 목적어를 받지 않아 has been risen 같은 수동형은 쓸 수 없어요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
The commission recommended that every newly constructed public building ____ with ramps and elevators so that wheelchair users can enter without assistance.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.

if 절은 과거(two decades ago) 일을 가정하지만 결과는 지금(today) 이야기라 혼합 가정법 would not be submerged 를 써요. would not have been submerged 는 과거 결과일 때 써요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
Archaeologists say what ____ them most was not the sheer size of the ancient settlement but how meticulously its streets had been planned.
빈칸 바로 뒤에 목적어 them 이 있으니 능동이고, 고고학자들이 '놀란' 일은 지난 일이라 astonished 가 맞아요. was astonished 는 뒤에 목적어를 둘 수 없어요.

Not only ____ cheaper to manufacture, but it can also be stored for months without refrigeration, a decisive advantage in remote regions.
Not only 가 문장 앞에 오면 주어와 동사 자리가 바뀌어요. 형용사 cheaper 가 보어라 be 동사가 앞으로 나온 is the new vaccine 이 맞아요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.

빈칸 뒤에 목적어가 없고 엘리베이터는 점검을 '받는' 쪽이라 수동태 must be inspected 예요. must inspect 는 엘리베이터가 점검하는 꼴이 돼요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
Officials hoped the new bus lanes would ____ congestion downtown, but traffic actually deteriorated as motorists avoided the narrowed streets and clogged the adjacent roads instead.
but 뒤에 오히려 더 막혔다는 결과가 오므로, 원래 바란 것은 정체를 '덜어 주는(alleviate)' 것이에요. aggravate(악화시키다)는 실제 결과 쪽이에요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
Because one report forecast robust growth while the other warned of a prolonged recession, analysts were struck by the ____ between two studies that had relied on identical data.
한쪽은 성장, 한쪽은 불황을 내다봤기 때문에 두 연구 사이의 '큰 차이(disparity)'가 눈에 띈 거예요. consistency·congruity·parity·affinity 는 모두 '같음, 어울림' 쪽이라 반대예요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
Because inspectors had detected perilous levels of toxins in the groundwater, the corporation, which had insisted for months that its factory was safe, finally ____ and admitted the danger.
독성 물질이 검출됐기 때문에 몇 달 버티던 회사가 결국 위험을 인정했으니 '털어놓다(came clean)'가 맞아요. stood its ground 는 계속 버틴다는 뜻이라 반대예요.

빈칸 (A), (B)에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
The fitness chain publicly promoted its new membership app as a way of (A) ____. Former employees, however, revealed that its real aim was (B) ____, since the app quietly logged members' locations and sold the data to advertisers.
profiting from members' data … helping members track workouts
helping members track workouts … improving gym safety
helping members track workouts … reducing staff costs
lowering membership fees … training new instructors
helping members track workouts … profiting from members' data
겉으로 내세운 목적(A)은 운동 기록 돕기이고, 위치를 몰래 모아 광고주에게 팔았다는 단서로 실제 목적(B)은 회원 정보로 돈 벌기(profiting from members' data)예요. however 가 겉과 속을 갈라요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
Reviewers lauded the historian's prose as ____, noting that even her most intricate ideas are conveyed in sentences of remarkable clarity and simplicity.
복잡한 생각도 아주 맑고 쉬운 문장으로 쓴다며 칭찬했으니 '맑고 투명한(limpid and transparent)'이 맞아요. 나머지는 어렵거나 장황하거나 꼬인 문체라 칭찬과 맞지 않아요.

improving passenger comfort … increasing seat capacity
increasing seat capacity … improving passenger comfort
reducing ticket prices … improving passenger comfort
improving passenger comfort … attracting business travelers
speeding up boarding … training cabin crew
겉으로 내세운 목적(A)은 승객 편안함(improving passenger comfort)이고, 얇은 좌석으로 줄을 두 개 더 넣었다는 단서로 실제 목적(B)은 좌석 수 늘리기(increasing seat capacity)예요. however 가 겉과 속을 갈라요.

how memory for songs fades with age
why listeners prefer melody to rhythm
how knowing something blinds us to others' ignorance

밑줄 친 말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
A <u>perspicacious</u> investor, she discerned the ominous signs in the company's ledgers months before the auditors did.
perspicacious 는 '통찰력이 있는, 눈치가 빠른'이라 sharp and insightful 과 가까워요. 감사인보다 몇 달 먼저 경고 신호를 알아챘다는 설명이 단서이고, slow and dull 과 naive and trusting 은 반대예요.

captious 는 '흠잡기 좋아하는, 트집 잡는'이라 picky and critical 과 같아요. '그런 사람조차 반대할 게 거의 없었다'는 흐름이 단서이고, relaxed and tolerant 는 반대예요.

written about topics that I loathed

부탁을 다 받아들이다 잠도 못 자고 기사까지 엉망이 됐으니 taken on more work than I could handle, 곧 감당할 수 있는 것보다 많은 일을 떠맡았다는 뜻이에요. 동료의 도움을 받았으니 도움을 거절했다는 말은 반대예요.

falling asleep during an important interview

Which of the following best describes the author's attitude toward digitizing cultural heritage?
supportive, but concerned about its costs and limits

파일 형식이 낡고 서버가 고장 나며 관리 비용이 프로젝트가 끝난 뒤에도 계속된다고 했으니 Digital archives need ongoing funding 로 볼 수 있어요. 큐레이터들은 오히려 원본을 지켜야 한다고 했어요.

밑줄 친 말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.

iconoclastic 은 '관습을 깨뜨리는, 우상 파괴적인'이라 bold and unconventional 과 가까워요. 오페라를 쇼핑몰로 옮겨 전통파를 화나게 했다는 설명이 단서이고, cautious and traditional 은 반대예요.

밑줄 친 말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
Many readers find the novel too <u>didactic</u>, since its characters habitually interrupt the narrative to lecture one another about the virtues of diligence.
didactic 은 '가르치려 드는, 훈계조의'라 preachy and lecturing 이 맞아요. 인물들이 이야기를 끊고 서로 성실함의 미덕을 설교한다는 설명이 단서이고, light and playful 은 반대예요.

밑줄 친 말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
The two researchers' <u>fortuitous</u> meeting on a delayed train culminated in a collaboration that eventually yielded a new treatment for burns.
fortuitous 는 '우연한, 뜻밖에 운이 좋은'이라 lucky and unplanned 가 맞아요. 연착된 기차에서 마주친 일이 좋은 결과로 이어졌다는 설명이 단서이고 planned and arranged 는 반대예요.

밑줄 친 말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
The tax code is so <u>arcane</u> that even many accountants rely on specialized software to decipher its rules for ordinary households.
arcane 은 '아는 사람만 아는, 난해한'이라 difficult and confusing 과 같아요. 회계사조차 전용 프로그램에 기댄다는 설명이 단서이고, simple and straightforward 는 반대예요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
The list of ingredients printed on the back of the package ____ several preservatives that the manufacturer had pledged to eliminate last year.
주어는 The list(단수)이고 of ingredients printed ~ package 는 꾸밈말이에요. 그래서 단수 동사 includes 가 맞아요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
When the railway between Liverpool and Manchester ____ in 1830, some skeptics feared that travel at such speeds would harm the human body.
in 1830 이라는 분명한 과거 시점이 있으니 단순 과거 opened 를 써요. 현재완료 has opened 는 과거 시점 부사와 함께 쓰지 않아요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
Fresh paint ____ until it has dried completely, or the surface will be marred by smudges that are difficult to remove.
빈칸 뒤에 목적어가 없고 페인트는 '만져지는' 쪽이라 수동태이고, not 은 조동사 바로 뒤에 와요. 그래서 should not be touched 예요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
After Saturday's loss, the coach ____ poor communication between the defenders rather than any single player's blunder.
blame A on B 는 'A 를 B 탓으로 돌리다'예요. 패배(A)를 수비수끼리의 소통 부족(B) 탓으로 돌렸으니 blamed the defeat on 이 맞아요. blame 뒤에 for 를 쓰려면 탓할 사람이 먼저 와야 해요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.

imperative 처럼 필요·당위를 뜻하는 형용사 뒤 that 절에는 (should) 동사원형이 와요. 결과는 '검증받는' 쪽이라 be verified 예요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.

빈칸 뒤에 목적어가 없고 안내서는 '쓰인' 쪽이라 수동의 분사구문 Written 이 맞아요. Writing·Having written 은 안내서가 직접 글을 쓴 것이 되어 어색해요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
The population of the capital is now nearly ____ of the second-largest city, a disparity that continues to widen every year.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
Rather than ____ the convoluted instructions, the revised manual merely added more technical jargon, leaving users even more bewildered than before.
설명서가 오히려 전문 용어만 늘려 사용자를 더 헷갈리게 했다는 대비(Rather than)이니, 원래 할 일은 지시를 '알기 쉽게 밝히는(elucidating)' 것이에요. obfuscating(흐리게 하다)은 실제 결과 쪽이에요.

빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.

포기하지 않았기 때문에(so) 한 해를 더 들여 제품을 고쳤다는 흐름이니 '포기하기(throw in the towel)'를 거부한 거예요.

빈칸 (A), (B)에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.

What is the passage mainly about?

According to the passage, what happens after the blocks are steeped in brine?

Which of the following is true according to the passage?

주어는 Consumers(복수)이고 who ~ period 는 꾸밈말이라 동사 자리가 비어 있어요. 단수형 receives·has received 는 수가 맞지 않아 will receive 가 맞아요.

Which of the following would make the best title for the passage?
The Ascendancy of the French Glass Industry

지식을 모아 누구나 쓰게 하려 한 디드로의 백과전서와 그것이 품은 생각을 다루니 Knowledge for Everyone: Diderot's Encyclopédie 가 맞아요. 지식은 소수의 것이 아니라고 했으니 A Book Written for a Privileged Few 는 반대예요.
According to the passage, how did some articles impugn the authority of the Church and the monarchy?

by cross-referencing harmless entries to daring ones
by publishing elaborate illustrations of royal palaces

몇몇 항목은 무해한 항목에서 비판적인 항목으로 이끄는 상호 참조로 권위를 문제 삼았다고 했으니 by cross-referencing harmless entries to daring ones 가 맞아요. 흔히 간접적(obliquely)이었다고 했으니 대놓고 혁명을 외쳤다는 말은 반대예요.
Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

장인의 지식을 진지하게 다룬 것이 '손일을 낮춰 보던 사회 질서'에 맞선 일이었다고 했으니 Manual labor had low status in France then 로 볼 수 있어요. 역사가들은 혁명과의 관계를 아직 다툰다고 했어요.
